title: Securing the Agentic Era: Rethinking API Trust for AI Agents
speaker: Anil Kolhe
summary: What happens when AI becomes autonomous, and more importantly, how do we make sure we can trust it? This session brings together STEM leadership, AI, API security, and enterprise engineering. Chief guest Kemal Akkaya, Professor & Chair of the Department of Computer Science at Virginia Commonwealth University and an IEEE Fellow, shares insights on STEM and computer science leadership. Anil Kolhe, Principal Engineer & Architect at Yodlee, follows with a technical talk on API Security by Design, architecting trust for autonomous AI agents and examining the security challenges emerging as AI systems become increasingly autonomous. This is more than a technical talk, it's a conversation about building the foundations of trust for the next generation of intelligent systems. Join ACM Richmond Chapter and IEEE Computer Society for this virtual event, open to the community.

title: The Invisible Weight of the Web
speaker: Shailesh Kadam
summary: The average webpage has grown 300% in a decade, and that weight now shows up on the bottom line — 53% of users abandon a page after a 3-second load, and every extra second of delay costs 7% in conversions. This session broke down where the bloat comes from (oversized images, bloated JS bundles, missing server-side compression) and walked through the next generation of compression tooling — Brotli and Zstandard for text and data, AVIF and WebP for images — along with a practical 4-week roadmap teams can use to audit, convert, and validate their way to a 40-60% reduction in page weight.

title: The License Performance Cost Trilemma: Why AI-Driven Database Operations Break Traditional Oracle Economic
speaker: Devendra Rajput
summary: As enterprises adopt AI-driven database management, they encounter an underappreciated three-way tradeoff between licensing exposure, performance, and cost. Based on peer-reviewed research and 20 years of enterprise Oracle experience across Exadata, RAC, and OCI, this session presents the trilemma framework, empirical findings from large-scale environments, and a practical, license-aware methodology for evaluating AI database tooling. The talk is designed to be accessible to a broad technical audience while offering depth for database and cloud practitioners.
